patch.value: Batch open backlog triage with bounded streaming and stable receipts
Implement open backlog selection, one run deadline, compact per-item streaming, content receipt reuse, stale inference protection, minimal projection and direct packed install acceptance.

value.author: codex-sol-implementation
value.text: Implementation scope: bounded open backlog selection and one deadline; compact streaming; full source hashes and redacted apply receipts; stale inference checks; smaller triage state; supported Ollama keep_alive; direct tarball acceptance. Existing reconciliation items remain owned by the orchestrator. Live model calls are waiting for baseline completion.

value.author: codex-sol-implementation
value.text: Inspected the host authoring contracts: streaming uses public writeStdout and suppressHostOutput, while SDK read output controls are static rather than an asynchronous item iterator. Ollama systemone accepts shared state plus named questions and no independent-state batch or streaming response. Reuse one boundary/client/catalog and one run AbortSignal across sequential item requests. The official TypeSafe SDK forwards additional request properties, so Ollama keep_alive uses its actual systemone wire field without a custom transport. Existing triage already used one systemOne call for four questions. Hosted opt-in and redirect refusal remain enforced.

value.author: codex-sol-implementation
value.text: Implementation uses complete untruncated source SHA-256 for receipt reuse, plus a redacted inference revision hash and expiry checked by the host mutation guard under the item lock. Source reuse ignores inferred type/priority and annotations so apply does not invalidate its receipt. Tests bind real scratch clients with createExtensionCommandSdk and initialize real trackers through PmClient.init, avoiding repeated CLI boot overhead and accidental package-workspace scope. Packed acceptance uses deterministic loopback HTTP and direct archive installation; real model acceptance remains separate and has not run.

value.author: codex-sol-implementation
value.text: Behavioral revert proof in a scratch package copy: preserved working source, changed only projectTriageState to the earlier broad projection and triageSourceHash to a hash of truncated projected input. Rebuilt dist with npm run build, then ran node --test test/triage-dist.test.ts unchanged: exit 1, 0 passed, 3 failed, 0 skipped or canceled. Failures were minimal wire evidence, routing-stable full-content identity, and repeat apply making two HTTP requests instead of one. Restored the two functions byte-for-byte, rebuilt dist and reran the same command: exit 0, 3 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped or canceled. No exports or tests were removed.

value.author: codex-sol-implementation
value.text: The linked real-tracker regression command passed 11 tests with zero failures, cancellations or skips. The host reported test-result tracking disabled; no project policy was changed. Whole-source coverage exposed one remaining generic host-error branch, now covered with deletion during inference. Packed acceptance uses deterministic loopback responses and direct archive installation for npm and native Bun; no live model request has been made.

value.author: codex-sol-implementation
value.text: Correction to the preceding coverage note: deletion during inference preserves the host item_deleted code; a separate strict ownership refusal exercises the code-less expected error fallback. Synthetic duplicate-description projection measured 4307 bytes before versus 2164 bytes after (49.76 percent smaller JSON state); this is input-size evidence, not live latency or token-use evidence. Live measurements remain owned by the orchestrator.

value.author: codex-sol-implementation
value.text: The final generic-error regression removes only a scratch source document while the deterministic HTTP response is pending. The real host raises a code-less missing-item error; the batch emits jev_triage_failure and writes no receipt. A separate SDK deletion case retains item_deleted. Both tests preserve native SDK behavior without PM mocks. Prior exploratory ownership fixtures were replaced rather than weakening coverage thresholds.

value.author: codex-sol-implementation
value.text: The host-linked command PM_AUTHOR=codex-sol-implementation pm --no-extensions test pm-jev-k8qe --run --progress passed its then-current 13 regressions, zero failed, canceled or skipped. Deleted/missing source cases were subsequently consolidated into one table-driven regression to preserve the existing zero-duplication gate; both native failure branches remain covered. The batch documentation is included in package files so the README link works for installed consumers.

value.author: codex-sol
value.text: Addressing PR 7 review thread 4240740980: separate stale installed-host receipt refusal from expiry. Build receipt hashes from the current complete source snapshot, set deadline_ms=0, assert refusal and no mutation, then verify the identical receipt with a future deadline is accepted. Prove sensitivity by disabling only the deadline condition in guardTriageMutation, rebuilding the packed artifact, and running the unchanged install acceptance test.

value.author: codex-sol
value.text: Installed-host expiry regression proof: in an isolated package copy changed only guardTriageMutation to remove Date.now() < Number(guard[2]), leaving the source-hash check intact. Rebuilt dist through npm run test:install and ran the byte-identical acceptance test: 0 passed, 1 failed, zero skipped/canceled, exit 1, with host accepted an expired triage receipt with matching current-source hashes. The stale-receipt refusal passed first. The unmodified guard passed the direct install acceptance 1/1, including unchanged source after expiry refusal and successful acceptance after changing only deadline_ms to a future value. Linked batch regressions passed 12/12. npm run release:check passed; Bun and isolated Git identity gates are pending. Existing linked-test result persistence is disabled, so evidence is recorded here.
